The scratchpad scrape material was consulted only to source the two real "beyond ten" karashynyard products (1629901938947 image ___14.jpg, 1636965991022 image ___15.jpg, their descriptions) used as test data in catalog.test.ts and products.test.ts. (b) catalog/products tests build the service as `createCatalogService({ source, shops: [{ adapter: { shop, fetchProducts }, snapshotKey }], snapshots: createSnapshotSource(dir), cache: createTtlCache({ ttlMs: 300000, now }), now })` with `shop = { key, name, url }` literals, and read "their 10 snapshot products" via `await createSnapshotSource(<repo>/data/shops).read(key)` (top-level await; `read` may be sync or async); (c) products.test.ts goes through `createApp({ catalog }).request(...)` as task 1.7 instructs and therefore does not import `./products` directly (the task's "Verify: imports ./products" line is not literally met; the red line for that file is the missing `../lib/cache`); (d) "Runtime switch to snapshot" lives in catalog.test.ts per task 1.6 but issues the scenario's literal `GET /api/products` via `createApp({ catalog: service })`; findings.issue: Scenario "Fixture page yields its products in page order" (and the comment in apps/api/src/shops/karashynyard.test.ts lines 7-9, and design.md D2) says each popup block carries "the same li_title__/li_price__ fields". In the committed fixture the popup <div class="t776__product-full js-product"> blocks carry only field="li_price__<lid>" (plus li_price_old__); their title is a bare <div class="t776__title ... js-product-name"> with no field attribute, and there is no li_descr__. The assertions are unaffected (a parser keyed on data-product-lid or li_price__ would still produce 8 or empty-name products and fail the 4-id check), but the description of the fixture is inaccurate.
